details: @zeppeliorg/wbails is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library whose installed code silently brands and fabricates forwarding metadata on the messages its users send. In lib/Socket/luxu.js — instantiated on every call to sendMessage in lib/Socket/messages-send.js — event, poll-result and album messages are stamped with hardcoded third-party channel identifiers: 120363421563597486@newsletter (newsletterName "D | 7eppeli-Exloration") and 120363399602691477@newsletter. The same messages receive forged delivery metadata: forwardingScore 99999, isForwarded: true, remoteJid "status@broadcast", a businessOwnerJid, and a synthetic disappearingMode with every initiatedBy flag (system, server, admin, bot, app, user) set true. Album messages additionally carry newsletterJid "0@newsletter" with newsletterName "WhatsApp". Recipients therefore see the caller's bot traffic as channel-forwarded content attributed to those channels instead of to the operator; the poll example in the package documentation passes only a placeholder channel JID ("1@newsletter"). Separately, package.json declares a dependency on cache-manager ^7.2.8, a version range that permits installation of the malicious cache-manager 7.2.10 release. The preinstall hook target engine-requirements.js only checks the Node.js major version. No credential, token or wallet access, no hidden command-and-control endpoint and no remote code execution were found in the package.
